toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check on interested sources (E2, E6, E3), then ACH across the five hypotheses; Kepner-Tregoe IS/IS NOT distinctions on X14 (Fennick vs Brackwater tags, counters/kiosks, Pelion and transfer tags)
output.brief:
The evidence points away from Tessaly and toward the tag stock. On 1 September check-in switched from Brackwater to Fennick tag stock, the same day the handler changed. Bags with Fennick tags fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% for August's Brackwater tags. Pelion's tags and Corvane's transfer tags stay near 1.3–1.4%. When counters briefly used Brackwater stock on 14–16 October, their failure rate fell to 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock stayed at 12%. That points to the tag stock, or how the printers are set for it, and not to the airport's readers or to Tessaly's crews. Those unreadable bags go to manual encoding and then miss the lateral cutoff.

I am fairly confident in the stock link. I can't yet say whether Fennick's stock is faulty or the printers just need different heat settings. I did not check mishandling cause codes or reconciliation data, so Tessaly's crews may still contribute somewhat.

Next: do not send the breach notice or withhold the fee. Switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater now, since about five weeks of stock is on hand. Then test Fennick stock and printer settings before making any claim against Fennick.
